, estimation, and control are addressed by model predictive control (MPC). A key MPC attribute is its receding-horizon approach, which allows the use of robust controllers even in scenarios where solving the infinite-horizon optimal control is computationally prohibitive, provided that a heuristic or suboptimal controller is available instead. However, implementing this framework requires solving an online moving-horizon robust controller, which suffers from restrictions imposed by robustness criteria. Specifically, $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ control fails to produce robust MPC solutions because it cannot incorporate uncertainty models. In contrast, eigenspace-based (EB) MPC offers significant advantages, including the ability to integrate diverse MPC objectives, reduced computational demands compared to standard MPC, and the capacity to handle structured uncertainties via eigenvalue assignment. Consequently, an infinite-horizon MPC based on the $K$-step prediction (P-MP) is proposed to enable MPC implementation for uncertain systems. In this framework, uncertain dynamics are approximated using eigenvalue assignment, and prediction models are generated based on these estimates to facilitate the use of prediction filters within an eigenvalue assignment scheme. To validate the approach, this paper presents a comparative analysis of P-MP against MPC and model-based model predictive control (MB-MPC) in terms of performance and computational efficiency.

presents a dual challenge for manual and automatic segmentation: the low contrast between the tumors and surrounding tissues, often exacerbated by poor visual quality, and the frequent presence of highly deformable normal anatomical structures that invades the tumor area. Since existing public datasets are unable to capture this difficulty, this paper introduces a new set of labeled slices from three additional abdominal scan sets that specifically include cases with vague or missing tumor-anatomy boundaries.
